statement: If as many odd numbers as we please be added together, and their multitude be odd, the whole will also be odd.
heath_proof: For let as many odd numbers as we please, AB, BC, CD, the multitude of which is odd, be added together; I say that the whole AD is also odd. Let the unit DE be subtracted from CD; therefore the remainder CE is even. [VII. Def. 7] But CA is also even; [IX. 22] therefore the whole AE is also even. [IX. 21] And DE is an unit. Therefore AD is odd. [VII. Def. 7]
ai_proof_text:
9.23
**Statement:** If as many odd numbers as we please be added together, and their multitude be odd, the whole will also be odd.

**Step 1.** Let AB, BC, CD be as many odd numbers as we please, their multitude being odd, and let them be added together so as to make up the whole AD. I say that AD is odd.

**Step 2.** If the multitude is a single number, the whole AD is that odd number itself and the statement holds at once. Suppose then that the multitude is greater than one, so that there is a last number CD with numbers AB, BC before it.

**Step 3.** Since CD is odd, it differs by a unit from an even number [D7.7]. Let the unit DE be subtracted from CD; then the remainder CE is even [D7.7].

**Step 4.** The multitude of the numbers AB, BC, CD is odd, and the multitude of the numbers AB, BC falls short of it by a unit (the number CD having been set aside); therefore the multitude of AB, BC is even [D7.7].

**Step 5.** Thus AB, BC are odd numbers whose multitude is even; therefore their sum AC is even [9.22].

**Step 6.** Since AC is even and CE is even, the whole AE, made up of the even numbers AC and CE, is even [9.21].

**Step 7.** But AD exceeds AE by the unit DE. Therefore AD differs by a unit from the even number AE, and so AD is odd [D7.7].

**Step 8.** Therefore, if as many odd numbers as we please be added together and their multitude be odd, the whole is also odd. Q.E.D.
